topicName: The Legal System in the UK

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The rule of law is a fundamental principle: no one is above the law, including the government. Laws must be clear, public, and applied equally to everyone.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Parliamentary sovereignty means Parliament is the supreme law-making body. No Parliament can bind its successors, and courts cannot overrule primary legislation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Statute law is written law passed by Parliament through the legislative process (Bill → Royal Assent → Act). Common law is developed through court decisions and judicial precedent.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Precedent: lower courts must follow decisions of higher courts in similar cases. This ensures consistency but can mean outdated rulings persist until overturned by a higher court or Parliament.
